/-!
# Conjecture 10.36

by G. A. Noskov

Is it true that $SL_n(\mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_r])$, for $n$ sufficiently large, is a group of
type $(FP)_m$?

Here a group $G$ is of type $(FP)_m$ if the trivial $\mathbb{Z}[G]$-module $\mathbb{Z}$ has a
projective resolution $\cdots \to P_1 \to P_0 \to \mathbb{Z} \to 0$ whose terms $P_i$ with
$i \le m$ are finitely generated. As the notebook says, this is the definition of type
$(FP)_\infty$ from its Problem 6.3, weakened by not imposing finite generation on the terms of
the resolution with numbers $> m$.

The notebook records an affirmative answer for $m = 0$, $n \ge 3$ (A. A. Suslin, 1977:
$SL_n(\mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_r])$ is generated by elementary matrices for $n \ge 3$, hence
finitely generated) and for $m = 1$, $n \ge 5$ (M. S. Tulenbaev, 1983; U. Rehmann and C. Soulé,
1976: these groups are finitely presented). In these remarks the notebook uses $(FP)_0$ for
finite generation and $(FP)_1$ for finite presentation. This is shifted by one from the
standard (Bieri) indexing used in `IsOfTypeFP` below, where $(FP)_0$ holds for every group,
$(FP)_1$ is finite generation, and finite presentation implies $(FP)_2$. Since the question
quantifies over all $m$, the two indexings give equivalent formalizations of the question.
The two solved cases are stated directly as finite generation and finite presentation.

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 10.36
* A. A. Suslin, *On the structure of the special linear group over polynomial rings*,
  Math. USSR Izvestiya **11** (1977), 221–238
* M. S. Tulenbaev, *The Steinberg group of a polynomial ring*,
  Math. USSR Sbornik **45** (1983), 139–154
* U. Rehmann, C. Soulé, *Finitely presented groups of matrices*, in: Algebraic $K$-theory
  (Proc. Conf., Northwestern Univ., Evanston, Ill., 1976), Lecture Notes in Math. **551**,
  Springer, Berlin, 1976, 164–169
-/

def IsOfTypeFP (G : Type) [Group G] (m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ P : ProjectiveResolution
      (ModuleCat.of (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ).asModule),
    ∀ i ≤ m, Module.Finite (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (P.complex.X i)
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is of type $(FP)_m$ if the trivial $\mathbb{Z}[G]$-module $\mathbb{Z}$ has a
projective resolution $\cdots \to P_1 \to P_0 \to \mathbb{Z} \to 0$ in which the modules
$P_i$ with $i \le m$ are finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}[G]$-modules.

This is the standard (Bieri) indexing: $(FP)_0$ holds for every group, $(FP)_1$ is equivalent
to finite generation, and finite presentation implies $(FP)_2$. The Kourovka Notebook's
$(FP)_m$ is $(FP)_{m+1}$ in this indexing.

justification.closest_existing_considered: CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution, Module.Finite, Module.Projective, Rep.trivial / Representation.asModule, groupCohomology infrastructure (none express finite generation of resolution terms).
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.36».IsOfTypeFP
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has the homological finiteness property FP_m for groups (or modules). Defined as: ∃ P : ProjectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ).asModule), ∀ i ≤ m, Module.Finite (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (P.complex.X i). Restricted to G : Type so that ℤ (in Type 0) and the group ring live in the same ModuleCat universe, which has enough projectives.

blocks.name: IsOfTypeFP
blocks.text:
/--
A group $G$ is of type $(FP)_m$ if the trivial $\mathbb{Z}[G]$-module $\mathbb{Z}$ has a
projective resolution $\cdots \to P_1 \to P_0 \to \mathbb{Z} \to 0$ in which the modules
$P_i$ with $i \le m$ are finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}[G]$-modules.

This is the standard (Bieri) indexing: $(FP)_0$ holds for every group, $(FP)_1$ is equivalent
to finite generation, and finite presentation implies $(FP)_2$. The Kourovka Notebook's
$(FP)_m$ is $(FP)_{m+1}$ in this indexing.
-/
def IsOfTypeFP (G : Type) [Group G] (m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ P : ProjectiveResolution
      (ModuleCat.of (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ).asModule),
    ∀ i ≤ m, Module.Finite (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (P.complex.X i)

blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to
$\langle x_1, \ldots, x_k \mid R \rangle$ for some $k$ and some finite set $R$ of relators in
the free group on $x_1, \ldots, x_k$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Group.FG (only finite generation), PresentedGroup, Algebra.FinitePresentation (rings, not groups).
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.36».IsFinitelyPresented
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no definition of a finitely presented group (rg for FinitelyPresented/Group.FP finds only ring/module finite presentation). Defined as ∃ (k : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin k))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G).

blocks.name: IsFinitelyPresented
blocks.text:
/--
A group $G$ is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to
$\langle x_1, \ldots, x_k \mid R \rangle$ for some $k$ and some finite set $R$ of relators in
the free group on $x_1, \ldots, x_k$.
-/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (k : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin k))),
    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsOfTypeFP.mono {G : Type} [Group G] {m m' : ℕ} (h : m ≤ m') (hG : IsOfTypeFP G m') :
    IsOfTypeFP G m := by
  obtain ⟨P, hP⟩ := hG
  exact ⟨P, fun i hi => hP i (hi.trans h)⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) :
    Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨k, rels, -, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  have : Group.FG (PresentedGroup rels) := Group.fg_iff.mpr
    ⟨Set.range PresentedGroup.of, PresentedGroup.closure_range_of rels, Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.toMonoidHom) e.surjective

  have : Group.FG (PresentedGroup rels) := Group.fg_iff.mpr
    ⟨Set.range PresentedGroup.of, PresentedGroup.closure_range_of rels, Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.toMonoidHom) e.surjective

blocks.docstring:
Is it true that $SL_n(\mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_r])$, for $n$ sufficiently large, is a group
of type $(FP)_m$?

Formalized as: for every $m$ and every number $r$ of variables, there is $N$ such that
$SL_n(\mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_r])$ is of type $(FP)_m$ for all $n \ge N$. The threshold $N$
may depend on both $m$ and $r$. `IsOfTypeFP` uses the standard indexing of $(FP)_m$; since $m$
ranges over all natural numbers, this is equivalent to the same question in the notebook's
indexing.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question with implicit quantifiers: for every m (and every number r of variables), there is N (depending on m, and either on r or uniform in r — the statement is ambiguous; known results are uniform in r) such that for all n ≥ N, SL_n(ℤ[x_1,…,x_r]) is of type (FP)_m (trivial ℤ[G]-module ℤ has a projective resolution with finitely generated terms in degrees ≤ m); the notebook's indexing is shifted by one from the standard Bieri convention (its (FP)_0 = finitely generated, (FP)_1 = finitely presented), which is immaterial here since m ranges over all naturals; formalize as answer(sorry) ↔ … with a bespoke FP_m definition and Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin n) (MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same content: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ m r, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, FP_m(SL(n, ℤ[x_1..x_r])), with the threshold allowed to depend on m and r (the literal reading; documented in the docstring). c02's bespoke IsOfTypeFP was chosen: it is the direct encoding (a Mathlib ProjectiveResolution of the trivial ℤ[G]-module ℤ in ModuleCat.{0} (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G), with Module.Finite in degrees ≤ m), G : Type so that categorical Projective = Module.Projective (Small.{0}) and the free module ℤ[G] is available. I verified separately that MonoidAlgebra.of ℤ G g acts as the identity on the encoded module. c01's Type* version puts resolution terms in ModuleCat.{0} over a Type-u ring, which is dubious for u > 0; c04/c06/c07/c08's Rep.trivial + toModuleMonoidAlgebra encoding is also correct but more indirect. Standard (Bieri) indexing is used; the notebook's index shift is immaterial since m ranges over all ℕ (FP_{m+1} ⇒ FP_m and m ↦ m+1 gives the converse). Docstring/references merged from c01/c05.

claims.decomposer_note: Solved special case (Suslin 1977: SL_n(ℤ[x_1,…,x_r]) = E_n(ℤ[x_1,…,x_r]) for n ≥ 3, hence finitely generated for all r), to be stated as research solved; under the notebook's convention (FP)_0 means finitely generated (standard FP_1), since standard FP_0 holds trivially for every group, so state it as finite generation for all r and all n ≥ 3.
claims.reviewer_why: Identical across candidates: Group.FG SL(n, MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ) for all r and all n ≥ 3, research solved (Suslin: SL_n = E_n for n ≥ 3, and E_n(ℤ[x_1..x_r]) is generated by the finitely many e_ij(1), e_ij(x_k) since n ≥ 3). c02's form (explicit (r n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) binders, SL(n, R) notation) used; the notebook's (FP)_0 = finite generation, as the decomposition table prescribes.

claims.reviewer_why: Stated as finite presentation for all r and n ≥ 5 (research solved; Tulenbaev 1983, Rehmann–Soulé 1976 'Finitely presented groups of matrices'), using c02's bespoke IsFinitelyPresented (∃ k, finite rels ⊆ FreeGroup (Fin k), PresentedGroup rels ≃* G). Finite presentation is what the cited papers prove and does not depend on the inferred index shift; c03's alternative (standard FP_2) is also true but weaker and less faithful to the cited results. The API lemma IsFinitelyPresented.isOfTypeFP_two records the link to the main predicate.

decomposition_objections.text: None substantive. The table correctly notes the ambiguity about whether the threshold is uniform in r; I chose the literal (non-uniform) reading. The m_zero/m_one variants are described in the table via the notebook's shifted indexing, which is consistent with the cited results; I followed that.

/--
A group $G$ is of type $(FP)_m$ if the trivial $\mathbb{Z}[G]$-module $\mathbb{Z}$ has a
projective resolution $\cdots \to P_1 \to P_0 \to \mathbb{Z} \to 0$ in which the modules

to finite generation, and finite presentation implies $(FP)_2$. The Kourovka Notebook's
$(FP)_m$ is $(FP)_{m+1}$ in this indexing.

def IsOfTypeFP (G : Type) [Group G] (m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ P : ProjectiveResolution
      (ModuleCat.of (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ).asModule),
    ∀ i ≤ m, Module.Finite (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (P.complex.X i)

/--

the free group on $x_1, \ldots, x_k$.

def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (k : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin k))),
    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G)

    IsOfTypeFP G m := by
  obtain ⟨P, hP⟩ := hG
  exact ⟨P, fun i hi => hP i (hi.trans h)⟩

  sorry

    ⟨Set.range PresentedGroup.of, PresentedGroup.closure_range_of rels, Set.finite_range _⟩

is finitely presented for every $r$ and every $n \ge 5$ (M. S. Tulenbaev, *Math. USSR
Sbornik* **45** (1983), 139–154; U. Rehmann, C. Soulé, *Lect. Notes Math.* **551** (1976),
164–169).
-/

items: Quantifier scope of 'n sufficiently large': formalized with the threshold N depending on both m and r (∀ m r, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N). The statement is ambiguous between this literal reading and a reading uniform in r (∀ m, ∃ N, ∀ r, ∀ n ≥ N); the known cases cited in the notebook happen to be uniform in r. The literal reading was chosen and documented in the theorem docstring.

Indexing of FP_m: IsOfTypeFP uses the standard Bieri indexing (FP_1 = finitely generated, finite presentation ⟹ FP_2). The notebook's (FP)_m corresponds to standard FP_{m+1}. The main statement uses IsOfTypeFP _ m rather than _ (m+1); the two are equivalent because m ranges over all naturals and FP_{m+1} ⟹ FP_m.

Type FP_m is defined via Mathlib's categorical ProjectiveResolution in ModuleCat (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) with the trivial module (Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ).asModule (verified that MonoidAlgebra.of ℤ G g acts trivially), requiring Module.Finite for the complex terms in degrees ≤ m. The definition is restricted to groups G : Type (as in other Kourovka files) to keep ℤ and ℤ[G]-modules in one universe with enough projectives.

m_one is stated as finite presentation (what Tulenbaev / Rehmann–Soulé actually prove and what the table identifies as the notebook's (FP)_1), rather than the weaker standard FP_2; both readings were permitted by the table.

Two sorried @[category API] lemmas (isOfTypeFP_one_iff_fg: FP_1 ↔ Group.FG; IsFinitelyPresented.isOfTypeFP_two: finitely presented → FP_2) and one proved monotonicity lemma (IsOfTypeFP.mono) were added as basic API for the bespoke definitions, documenting the relation between the notebook's convention and the standard one. These are standard textbook facts (Bieri; Brown, Cohomology of Groups VIII.4).
AMS tags: 20 for the main open question; 19 20 for the solved variants whose proofs go through algebraic K-theory (Suslin's normality/stability, K_2-stability).

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities in the source: (1) 'for n sufficiently large' — formalized pointwise (N may depend on m and r), the literal reading with r a fixed parameter of the ring; the stronger uniform-in-r reading (∀ m, ∃ N, ∀ r, ∀ n ≥ N) was not stated, and all candidates made the same choice. (2) The notebook's (FP)_m indexing is shifted by one from Bieri's (its (FP)_0 = finitely generated, (FP)_1 ≈ finitely presented), inferred from the cited solved cases; the main statement is invariant under this shift because m ranges over all ℕ, and the solved variants are stated concretely as finite generation and finite presentation. (3) r = 0 (the ring ℤ) is included; harmless since SL_n(ℤ) is of type FP_∞. Final file composed mainly from c02 with docstrings/references from c01/c05 and IsFinitelyPresented.fg proof from c05; includes a proved monotonicity lemma, a proved 'finitely presented ⇒ finitely generated' lemma, and two sorry'd textbook API lemmas (FP_1 ↔ Group.FG; finitely presented ⇒ FP_2; Brown, Cohomology of Groups VIII.4–5) following repository precedent for sorry'd category API statements. Compiles with only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings. Candidates' decomposition objections (FP_2 ≠ finite presentation for arbitrary groups) are correct and were respected by choosing finite presentation for m_one.
statement:
Is it true that $SL_n({\Bbb Z}[x_1,\ldots
,x_r])$, for $n$ sufficiently large, is a group of type $(FP)_m$ (which is defined in the same way as $(FP)_{\infty}$ was defined in 6.3, but with that weakening that the condition of being finitely generated is not imposed on the terms of the resolution with numbers $ > m$). An affirmative answer is known for $m=0$, $n \geq 3$ (A. A. Suslin, Math. USSR Izvestiya, 11 (1977), 221–238) and for $m=1$, $n \geq 5$ (M. S. Tulenbayev, Math. USSR Sbornik, 45 (1983), 139–154; U. Rehmann, C. Soulé, in: Algebraic $K$-theory, Proc. Conf., Northwestern Univ., Evanston, Ill., 1976, $($Lect. Notes Math., 551), Springer, Berlin, 1976, 164–169).
